lesson.title: Our First Three Letters: ੳ, ਅ, ੲ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: The Punjabi alphabet is called Gurmukhi. Every Gurmukhi primer begins the same special way: with three letters that don't make their own sound by themselves. Instead, they carry every vowel sound the alphabet has. Today we'll meet all three.

ੳ (ura) looks like a hook with a tail. ਅ (aira) has a tall straight line with a loop. ੲ (iri) curves like a wave. Say each name slowly with your grown-up: oo-raa... ai-raa... ee-ree. These three letters always come first because every other vowel sound in Gurmukhi is written by adding a small mark to one of them.
Great work! You've met the very first letters every Gurmukhi reader learns. Next time, we'll start adding the marks that turn these three letters into different vowel sounds.

objectives: Recognize and name the three Gurmukhi vowel-bearer letters: ੳ (ura), ਅ (aira), ੲ (iri)
Understand that these three letters carry vowel sounds rather than having one fixed sound of their own
materialsNeeded: Optional: a Gurmukhi primer (Painti Akhari) chart, if you have one at home
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Show the child each letter one at a time — ੳ, then ਅ, then ੲ — and say its name aloud together three times.
2. Ask the child to describe what each letter looks like in their own words (a hook, a tall line with a loop, a wave). This builds visual memory before writing practice.
3. Trace each letter in the air with a finger before picking up a pencil.
4. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter in the box, then try writing it once more on the practice line underneath.
5. Close by saying all three names together in order: ura, aira, iri — this is the order every Gurmukhi primer uses, so it's worth repeating often.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one letter per sitting rather than all three at once; come back to the others another day
Ready for more: ask the child to find these three letters if they see any Gurmukhi writing around the house or at the Gurdwara
For a child who already recognizes the letters, have them try writing all three from memory before tracing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — there is no right/wrong answer beyond correct letter formation. Check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Letter recognition and formation are the foundation every later Punjabi reading and writing skill builds on, matching how Gurmukhi is traditionally introduced in Punjabi primers (the Painti Akhari sequence).

generationData.instructions: Trace each letter, say its name out loud, then write it once more on your own.
